cards.explanation: The answer is the glory of God. Verse 1 says, "The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of His hands." The sky is not just sitting up there looking pretty. It's pointing at the One who made it. Friends, that's the best sign anybody ever hung over a bakery, and it's free for everyone.

The answer is day after day and night after night. David says, "Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge." That's a sky that never takes a day off. No weekends, no holidays, no sick days. I'd love that work ethic on a Monday morning.

The answer is with no sound at all. Verse 3 says it plainly: "Without speech or language, without a sound to be heard…" So the sky speaks, and you can't hear a thing. Friends, that's the quietest sermon ever preached, and its voice still goes out into all the earth (Psalm 19:4).

The answer is earth. Verse 4 says their voice "…has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world." All the earth, friends. Not just one town, one people or one bakery. A message with no sound that still reaches the ends of the world has some serious range.

The answer is True. Verse 5 says the sun is "Like a bridegroom emerging from his chamber…" Picture a man stepping out on his wedding day, and now picture the sun doing it every morning. That's a grand entrance, friends, and I wish my entrance to the bakery got that kind of attention.

The answer is rejoicing to run his course. David says the sun is "…like a champion rejoicing to run his course…" Rejoicing, friends. That champion is not dragging his feet to the starting line. He's happy to be running.

The answer is False. David says "nothing is deprived of its warmth." The sun makes its whole run from one end of the heavens to the other, and not one thing gets skipped. Even the spot in the yard where the dog lies down gets covered.

The answer is that it revives the soul. Verse 7 says, "The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul…" Perfect and reviving, friends. It's not a heavy thing that drains you. It's something that brings you back to life.

The answer is light. Verse 8 says, "the commandments of the LORD are radiant, giving light to the eyes." Radiant and giving light, friends. It's like somebody finally flipped the switch in a dark room. I spent years in the back of a dark junk drawer, so believe me, light matters.

The answer is forever. Verse 9 says, "The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever…" Forever, friends. Everything else in my kitchen wears out eventually, even my best mixing bowl. David says this one doesn't, because it endures forever.
The answer is False. David says, "the judgments of the LORD are true, being altogether righteous." Altogether, friends! That word doesn't leave a single crumb of "partly" on the counter.

The answer is False. David calls them "…more precious than gold…" and "…sweeter than honey…" Those are things people want, not things people drag around. The picture is of something rich and sweet that David treasures.

The answer is True. Verse 11 says, "By them indeed Your servant is warned; in keeping them is great reward." David says the LORD's words warn him, and that great reward is found in keeping them. Friends, that's worth knowing in any kitchen.

The answer is that he asks God to cleanse him from hidden faults. David prays, "Cleanse me from my hidden faults." He just asked, "Who can discern his own errors?" so he asks God to cleanse the faults he may not even see. That's an honest prayer, friends. I think it's a good one to borrow.

The answer is that he prays they will not rule over him. David says, "Keep Your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me." He doesn't want sin sitting in charge of his life. Friends, that's a prayer worth praying every morning.

The answer is True. David says, "Then I will be blameless and cleansed of great transgression." It follows his prayer for God to keep him from willful sins. Friends, it's good news at the end of a serious prayer.

The answer is pleasing. David prays, "May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing in Your sight, O LORD…" Both the words he says out loud and the thoughts he keeps inside. Friends, that covers everything, even the stuff I mutter at a burnt batch.
The answer is my Rock and my Redeemer. The psalm ends with "…O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer." Two names, and David finishes his whole prayer on them. I think that's a strong place to land, friends.
